_note: The DECLARED BLIND ZONE of every directory walk in tools/gates, and the only thing that may
be invisible to a hard light. JSON takes no comments, so this is where this file is explained.
WHY IT EXISTS. Four doors can hide a path from a gate: .gitignore, ignorePatterns in
.oxlintrc.jsonc, exclude in a tsconfig, and testPathIgnorePatterns in jest.config.mjs. 'I
narrowed an include and everything went green' is a real way to pass, so L-visible counts what
is hidden under packages/, apps/ and e2e/ NUMERICALLY against git ls-files and refuses anything
this file does not declare. walk() in tools/gates/lights/_shared.mjs skips a path for exactly
one declared reason: an entry here. The predicate (isExcluded) lives in the same module that
reads this file, so the blind zone and the light guarding it read ONE file through ONE reader.
THE FOURTH DOOR HIDES, IT DOES NOT NARROW. jest.config.mjs can hide a path two ways, and they
belong to two different lights. testPathIgnorePatterns (and modulePathIgnorePatterns) hide a
path that otherwise matches, and that is this door. A NARROWED testMatch hides a test file by
never claiming it, and that is L-orphans, which counts every test file against the projects
that match it and refuses a file matched by none. Splitting them is deliberate: one light
cannot be the authority on both 'what is hidden' and 'what is claimed' without its own numbers
becoming unfalsifiable.
ENTRIES HOLDS ONE, AND IT IS THE ONE THIS FILE PREDICTED. Until 2026-11-02 the list was empty:
no tsconfig in this repository has an 'exclude' key (measured), jest.config.mjs declares no
testPathIgnorePatterns and no modulePathIgnorePatterns, and of .oxlintrc.jsonc:59-66's six
patterns only coverage/ existed, at the repository root and not under those three roots. CHQ-003
gave apps/web its first build script, so `vite build` produced apps/web/dist and L-visible
refused it by name — the behaviour the paragraph that stood here described in advance. It is
declared below rather than un-hidden, because a build output is derived state: it is rewritten by
every build, it is reproduced by `pnpm --filter @cheq/web build`, and committing it would make
the repository hold two copies of the same source. TWO doors hide it and both are named: it is
matched by .gitignore's `dist/` and by .oxlintrc.jsonc's `**/dist/**`, and an entry claiming only
one of them is a fail.
WHAT NEVER NEEDS AN ENTRY. A '.'-prefixed segment (.git, .ci, .pnpm) and node_modules are
already invisible to every tool in this toolchain, so declaring one would change nothing;
isExcluded reports them as self-hidden and L-visible does not count them. That list is a
frozen constant in CODE (SELF_HIDDEN in lights/_shared.mjs) and deliberately not a field here:
a configurable self-hidden list would be a second door, and the whole point of this file is
that there is one. Measured, and the reason it matters: apps/web/node_modules is under apps/
and is hidden by .gitignore:2.
ENTRY SHAPE, checked by manifestProblems() in lights/_shared.mjs:
{ "path": "<repo-relative literal path>",
"doors": ["gitignore" | "oxlint-ignorePatterns" | "tsconfig-exclude" | "jest-ignorePatterns"],
"why": "<one sentence>" }
A path matches an entry when it equals it or lies under it. NO GLOBS: a glob here would be a
small language nobody can audit, and 'which files does this hide' would stop being answerable
by reading. Naming the doors is what lets L-visible compare the declaration with what it
finds, so an entry that claims one door while a second also hides the path is a fail.

entries.why: Vite's build output for the SPA — derived from apps/web/src on every `pnpm --filter @cheq/web build`, synced into the S3 bucket by infra/, and never a source anything should check or commit.
